subject: Interaction custody scope, subprocessor migration plan, and DPA alignment
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medinova.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Medinova Procurement <procurement@medinova.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify custody & no-training scope for chat transcripts + subproc move

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. Before procurement takes this to legal, we need a concise clarification on two items for our DPA redline: 1) custody and IP for "interactions" (chat transcripts + structured prompts/metadata) — can Redwood commit to a no-training/no-derivative use for those interactions from our tenant? We need the language to be explicit (no internal model improvement, no derivative rights). 2) a planned subprocessor migration: you mentioned one of your analytics subprocessors (AtlasCloud) is moving certain processing from the EU to US in Q3. We need to understand timing, any cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs), and whether KMS residency or key escrow will change.

If you can send a short statement we can include as an appendix to the DPA (and any current inventory + high-level migration window), that would speed procurement. Attaching a sample redline from our side for context.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Compliance, Medinova Health

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify custody & no-training scope for chat transcripts + subproc move

Sam — good to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. High-level answers below; I attached a concise operational statement that your legal team can paste into the DPA appendix.

1) No-training / interaction custody: Redwood can commit that tenant interaction data (chat transcripts, prompt text, structured metadata, and ephemeral KV) will not be used for model training or model improvement for hosted customer-facing models unless a customer opts in. That commitment covers both upstream model training and fine-tuning pipelines. We also confirm no transfer of derivative IP back to Medinova unless explicitly negotiated (we provide output under the standard usage license).

- Operational notes we include in the appendix: data retention windows for ephemeral KV (default 24 hours, configurable); prompt/response logs used for billing/analytics are pseudonymized and stored distinctly from model training archives; export options (SFTP, API) for customers who require custody.

2) Subprocessor migration (AtlasCloud): AtlasCloud is planning a phased migration of analytics processes from the Frankfurt region to a US-based analytics cluster between Aug 15 — Sep 30, 2028. We will:
- Maintain SCC-based transfers for EU->US processing and update our subprocessor addendum when the move is complete.
- Offer a KMS routing option: for customers requiring EU-only key residency we can route encryption keys to an EU-managed KMS (requires an onboarding checklist).
- If KMS residency cannot be achieved for analytics workloads, we will provide an operational proof (audit report + ephemeral processing attestation) for customers to rely on.

I've looped in David (privacy counsel) and Kimberly (ops) for any contractual language and technical/ops attachments. I attached: DPA_Redline_v3 (our redline with the explicit no-train appendix), subprocessor-inventory-Jul2028.csv (csv, 12KB), and an onboarding checklist for SFTP + KMS routing.

Next steps we propose: 1) Medinova legal reviews our appendix + redline; 2) procurement confirms onboarding route (SFTP export vs API); 3) if EU-KMS is required, we schedule a short runbook call next week.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Forwarding quick technical & legal clarifications for the thread.

On Mon, 24 Jul 2028 at 10:04 AM marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> (see Marissa's note and attachments)

Sam — a couple of practical commitments we can make now and a few that need a brief ops checklist:

- Commitments we can accept in DPA: explicit no-training/no-derivative clause for tenant interactions; explicit statement that prompt/response ownership is retained by the tenant (we license outputs to customers, we don't claim derivative ownership).
- Operational constraints: to maintain the "no-training" promise we require (a) a tenant-level flag at onboarding to opt-out of any capture-to-training pipelines and (b) a short attestation from the customer if they later request exports for debugging (so we can log the export intent).
- Subprocessor migration specifics: AtlasCloud's migration will not touch core inference routing or KV cache that serves live inference — it's an analytics pipeline (billing and usage analytics, aggregated telemetry). That said, the telemetry may include hashed prompt identifiers; we will keep telemetry hashed and unlinkable to PII.

Jonas, can you confirm the technical route for EU-KMS key routing? Kimberly, please confirm the onboarding checklist fields we should add for procurement (SCCs, dataflow diagrams, evidence pack timeline).

Thanks,
David Kim
